statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39883 (GO-2026-5426, GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx): the host ID detector in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource ran the BSD kenv command by bare name, so on DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris a kenv placed earlier in PATH could run in the application. The BSD reader, hostIDReaderBSD, is selected only by sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go, whose build constraint names those platforms; v1.43.0 calls /bin/kenv instead: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8113, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426. Read the Go build information and the function table of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index, every entry with the same source commit and installed size as 2.19.1-r0; the copy the repository serves was read. Every Go program in every build is built for GOOS=linux. /usr/bin/build links go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource, and the function table of every one contains the Linux reader, (*hostIDReaderLinux).read, which reads /etc/machine-id or /var/lib/dbus/machine-id and runs no command, but no build contains (*hostIDReaderBSD).read, the only code that runs kenv, or resource.New, the function the advisory lists. The vulnerable code is not in these programs. Builds before 2.20.0-r2 link go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.38.0 or v1.40.0; 2.20.0-r2 and later link v1.43.0 or newer.
